comparison: Both strongly support the finding that TADs are preserved after cohesin removal (C4, C31, C32, C33, C96). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence from two cell lines and methodological robustness, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding as 'convincing' and 'thorough.'

Perfect agreement on TAD-like structures at single-cell level without cohesin (C9, C79-C82, C84, C86). Both evaluations highlight the computational predictions' agreement with experimental imaging data and describe the approach as powerful and validated.

Both support cross-cell-line robustness (C11, C99). OpenEval notes consistency across cell types but flags universality claim as somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers accept the multi-dataset analysis without challenging the robustness claim.

Strong agreement on enhancer-promoter loops at TAD boundaries (C10, C90-C92, C94, C95, C100). Both evaluations support the finding, though OpenEval notes functional interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly state this analysis 'strengthens the authors' claim' and provides 'biological context.'

Both strongly support epigenetic switches as a mechanism for TAD preservation (C6, C45, C51, C62, C66-C68, C97). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative simulation data, while peer reviewers note this 'challenges current dogma' and is mechanistically confirmed by CCM modeling.

Divergent evaluations on physical boundaries (C7, C52-C55, C60-C61, C63, C98). OpenEval finds the mechanism well-supported by simulation data. However, peer reviewers express uncertainty about causality and definition, with the editor noting 'it is unfortunately still unclear whether physical boundaries...are a consequence of preserved TADs, or whether preserved TADs are caused by the physical boundaries.'

Both support model validation (C35, C37-C39, C70, C102). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative metrics (PCC=0.83, TAD size agreement) demonstrating simulation-experiment agreement. Peer reviewers describe the theoretical approaches as 'state-of-the-art' and 'powerful means to generate 3D structures.'

Both accept methodological limitations acknowledgment (C34, C42, C64). OpenEval praises this as good scientific practice. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the transparency about methodological dependencies without contesting it.

Both support enhanced compartmentalization finding (C76). OpenEval notes consistency with prior literature and structural analysis. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this result as aligned with established knowledge without challenge.

Partial overlap on epigenetic switches preserving TADs (C66-C68). OpenEval focuses on experimental validation of simulation predictions. Peer result R2 addresses broader epigenetic mechanism including additional claims (C45, C51, C62, C97) not in OpenEval R5.

Minimal overlap on combined mechanisms (C73, C75). OpenEval R6 emphasizes HIPPS validation and the necessity of combining epigenetic switches with physical boundaries. Peer R3 focuses on uncertainty about physical boundaries' causal role, representing different aspects of the same general topic.

Minimal overlap on HIPPS method (C70). OpenEval R6 validates HIPPS methodology and its combination of mechanisms. Peer R6 broadly supports computational approaches as 'state-of-the-art' including HIPPS among other methods.

Minimal overlap on methodological validation (C101-C102). OpenEval R13 specifically highlights HIPPS advantages and imaging validation. Peer R6 provides broader support for computational approaches without specifically addressing HIPPS advantages.

Minimal overlap on TAD-calling algorithm discordance (C64). OpenEval R11 documents method-dependent variations as important methodological finding. Peer R8 implicitly accepts methodological caveats without specifically addressing algorithm discordance.

OpenEval supports the conceptual conclusion that single-cell structures explain ensemble TAD preservation (C65). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this integrative conceptual claim.
OpenEval supports boundary probabilities as alternative TAD identification method (C59). No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific methodological validation.
OpenEval notes independent computational support from Conte et al. 2020 (C83). No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific citation or cross-model validation.

OpenEval rates functional interpretation as uncertain/speculative (C93), noting it requires additional experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this functional speculation.
